else.title: Conditional expression
else.doc: In the canonical `IfTerm`, the condition is serialized as a Formula after Boolean lifting. `TRUE_ONLY` selects `then`, `FALSE_ONLY` selects `else`; `BOTH` yields `CONFLICTED_CONDITION`, `NEITHER` keeps missing/external issues without selecting a branch. A bare proposition in a data conditional is a static error, suggesting `established`, `supported`, `conflicted`, or another status test.

emit.title: Definition
emit.doc: **Parameters.** The `params` section is mandatory and unique; parameter names are unique. Parameter types are a closed list.

empirical.title: Missing data
empirical.doc: The negative-literal holder (DECISION-0353 §2, errata E-0235). A bare negative literal in a body — `when not p(x)`, per §66 the same as `established(not p(x))` — requires `p(x)` to have status `FALSE_ONLY`, obtainable ONLY from an explicit negative: a §99 negative rule head, a §71 negative assertion, an accepted `refutes` support §78.2.2, or §70 closure with `derive_explicit_negative`.

entity.title: Nominal entity types
entity.doc:
Declares a nominal type: identity is the pair (type, stable id); equal ids in two types never mix.

Declare only intrinsic immutable payload; temporal or disputable traits belong in relations. Address pinned individuals with entity_ref.

entity_labels.doc: `entity_labels` carries the §218 labels of a case entity addressed by StableId: `entity_labels "<StableId>" { label …; }`. It declares no entity, asserts no fact, and creates no constant.

entity_ref.title: Nominal entity types
entity_ref.doc: `entity_ref(id)` contextually receives the expected nominal entity type. Identity is the pair `(nominal_type, stable_id)`; the same string in `Person` and `Company` does not make the values equal. In `core-production` the entity ID must be an absolute IRI/URN or a resolved package/case-scoped StableId. Anonymous/mutable entity objects do not exist.

entrenchment.title: Entrenchment
entrenchment.doc:
Shields one source passage over a time window: a locator plus its validity interval.

The locator shields itself and its /-children only: article/2 covers /paragraph/7, never /20. A touching revision op is refused (E5301).

Declares a closed set of named members: the total vocabulary of one choice.

Closed means closed: maps over an enum prove totality (E1326 on a miss). Members are bare names, compared by identity.

established.title: Status tests
established.doc: `established(P)` returns a Boolean data value. In a rule body, a bare `P` is shorthand for requiring `P == TRUE_ONLY`. In Core 0.1 a status-test operand is a ground/groundable **literal**, not an arbitrary compound formula; compound status is expressed as a Boolean combination of status-tests. This preserves a well-defined producer barrier and closure key.

establishes.title: Decision unit — support, not document or fact
establishes.doc: §78.1 describes the acceptance phase as an implementation duty but specifies neither the policy's holder, its inputs, nor the form of its decision. This section defines **one** executable profile. The profile is core machinery; the policy itself is package data (CLIR rules), and no specific policy rule lives in the implementation.

evaluate.title: `evaluate` — query
evaluate.doc: `evaluate` names the standard §172 query over a proposition or term whose value is requested (`DATA` §174.1). A test allows SEVERAL queries per case (errata E-0127): each `expect` refers to the nearest preceding `evaluate`, i.e. addresses the fields of ONE result — its own step. An expectation before the first `evaluate`, and a step with no `expect` at all, are rejected as `LDC-E1316`.

evaluative.title: Relations
evaluative.doc: `Kind` is metadata for analysis and policies. By itself it does not change truth semantics.

event.title: Event declaration
event.doc:
Desugars to an immutable nominal entity with id and typed fields; executable use wants one canonical time interval.

Instances are immutable; a correction creates a new version with provenance (§81.1). Prefer entity_ref when a pinned snapshot supplies the payload.

every.title: Recurrence sugar
every.doc: **Bounds and anchor — the `over` clause.** The schedule is counted from the START of the `over` interval in `every` steps; occurrence `k` (zero-indexed) occupies the half-open interval `[start + k·P, start + (k+1)·P)`, clipped at the end of `over`. Step `P` is a `CalendarPeriod` or `Duration` (§84); a calendar step is built by `add_calendar_period` (§84.2) and does not read the calendar (§85).

evidence.title: Evidence declaration
evidence.doc:
Declares a case document: a stable id over a typed schema with provenance fields.

Evidence is case input, not program: in a package it warns (E1314) and is refused without status (E1208). The core never derives admissibility from a count.

exact.title: Definition
exact.doc: Exact definitions do not apply contraposition. Use an exact or necessary definition to declare its institutional predicate; a one-way derivation is an explicit relation plus a strict rule.

exactly_one.title: Interpretation group
exactly_one.doc: Selection policy §155: choose exactly one reading from the group.

exclude.title: Extends
exclude.doc: A reference inside `extends` is of the same kind as one inside `alternatives`, and may be qualified (`extends pkg::Baseline`, §23/§24). `exclude`, however, stays local per §152: it removes the same expansion that `include` introduces.

exclusive.title: Deontic head `emit`
exclusive.doc: **Head composition.** The modality is `duty` or `prohibition` (DECISION-0209 R6; `liberty`, `power`, `immunity` are out of the 0.2 profile, `LDC-E1335`). The template path is a `generated_ref` of the form `<rule path>/norm` (§279.2.4).

exercise.title: Power
exercise.doc: A `power` describes the ability to create a legal effect upon valid exercise.

exists.title: Finite relation comprehensions
exists.doc: `collect all value: T, binder: U where F` allows additional existential local binders in the generator. Only `value` enters the collection; `binder` distinguishes solutions with the same value and is not free outside. This is needed, for example, when two different ownership positions carry the same share.

expand.title: Instance
expand.doc:
Instantiates a named expansion: binds its parameters to local relations and values.

Name the expansion first, then the instance, and label it (E1339 without one). Bind every parameter the expansion declares.

A closed generation profile: params plus emit rules that generate nodes with stable ids, labels and anchors.

expect.title: `expect` — result-field expectation
expect.doc: `expect` addresses fields of the result document (§174), not program facts. The field vocabulary is CLOSED and extended only additively. Operators are `==` and `!=`; ordering comparisons are undefined, since none of the enums are ordered and `truth_status > NEITHER` is meaningless for any of them.

expired.title: PositionInstance statuses
expired.doc: Condition 3 of `evaluate` applies to every normative node with anchors (`rule`, `norm_template`, `constraint`, `priority_rule`, `assertion`; errata E-0095): a node whose dating anchors ALL point to editions inapplicable at legal time under the lifecycle machine of §31 (`closed` | `suspended` | `not_yet`) takes no part in evaluation — the same as a rule outside `effective` under §87 (condition 4).

exports.doc:

extends.doc: `extends` creates a set composition, not a mutation. `exclude` must be explicit and visible in the provenance.

external.title: External data access
external.doc: The source language has no HTTP/SQL/file-read operator. Access goes through a declared capability and a snapshot binding, which ensures sandboxing, auditability, and reproducibility.

false.doc:
- `version` — the same EXACT version as in the string form: `import` checks against it (`LDC-E1111`, section 23), and it is what the lockfile pins (section 11). The string form is shorthand for a table with a single `version`; the meaning of the entry does not depend on the form;
- `registry` — the publisher the dependency was taken from.

fiction.title: Fiction
fiction.doc:
Deems an institutional fact true when its conditions hold: the law treats it as decided.

Strength after the name is mandatory: Core never picks one for you. A fiction concludes institutional facts, never empirical ones.

finishes.title: `law.std.time`
finishes.doc: The fifth and sixth rows are TERMS, not predicates: `before`/`after`/`during`/`overlaps`/`contains` return Boolean and construct nothing, whereas these nine produce values (`Date` for steps and bounds, `Integer` for measurements and weekday).

first.title: Decision tables
first.doc: `first` and `multiple` preserve source order. `collect` orders matching rows by canonical row ID; `multiple` keeps duplicates. `unique` must prove pairwise non-overlap. `any` allows overlap only with canonically identical output; unproven overlap is not carried into runtime and yields `LDC-E8304 UNSUPPORTED_FEEL`.

for.title: Finite domains
for.doc: Binds variables in rules (§52), iterates emit/premise expansion slots (§279.1), or names the factors subject (§276.2), according to context.

forall.title: Finite domains
forall.doc: Permitted in a representation profile, but not executable without a domain provider.

forbearance.title: Forbearance sugar
forbearance.doc: `achieve F during W;` sets a goal of achieving `F` within window `W`, while `maintain F during W;` sets a goal of maintaining `F` throughout it. These short forms inside `duty` are equivalent to full `goal achievement`/`goal maintenance` blocks with `condition F; window W;` fields (DECISION-0185).

format.title: Calendar snapshot
format.doc: `Calendar` must be immutable and versioned. In authoring syntax, `content_hash` means the digest of the **calendar dataset's content**, not the semantic hash of the CLIR node. The compiler computes the canonical node's own `contentHash` separately.

fragment.title: Fragment
fragment.doc:
Pins one addressable passage inside an edition: kind, locator and fixed text.

A fragment needs a stable id: the article number is locator metadata, never identity by itself.

version.doc:

CalendarPeriod.title: `CalendarPeriod`
CalendarPeriod.doc: v1 returns a **day count** (`Integer`), not a `CalendarPeriod` carrying a unit: a unit-bearing carrier would need algebra over inverse units (`1/day` for a daily rate), which v1 lacks (§49: multiplication only by a scalar). The unit stays visible in the function name.

CardinalityError.title: Built-in data types
CardinalityError.doc: `Rational` (errata E-0005) is an exact rational value: the result type of exact division (§58) and permitted internal arithmetic (§18); canonical serialization represents it as an irreducible fraction. **The carrier has no bit-width limit** (errata E-0159); protection against unbounded consumption is the §238 counters, and exceeding them yields `RESOURCE_LIMIT` with no partial result.

Collective.title: Collective and diffuse rights
Collective.doc: Core allows a `Collective` beneficiary, but a detailed model of an indeterminate class of persons requires the standard profile.

CountryCode.title: `law.std.data`
CountryCode.doc: `Jurisdiction` (errata E-0039) — the jurisdictional-binding type: §54 prints `const KZ: Jurisdiction = Jurisdiction { code: "KZ" };` as the canonical `const` example, §89 declares it as the first field of `EvaluationContext`, and `spec/examples/kz/social-code-art175.law` uses it as an institutional relation parameter.

Court.title: Evaluation of alternatives
Court.doc: If the context does not select exactly one alternative under `exactly_one`, the evaluator returns `INTERPRETATION_REQUIRED`.

Currency.doc:

Option.title: Built-in data types
